name: Technical utilitarian
philosophy: Help people understand state, compare information and act with confidence. Precision is the source of character; reduce effort before adding decoration.
influences: Operational tools, instrument panels and information-rich workspaces. Product category is not a fixed visual style: a technical interface can still have a distinctive brand.
characteristics: Clear separation of context, controls and results
typography: Choose distinguishable 0/O and 1/l/I, good punctuation and tabular numerals. Use proportional text for prose and mono only where token alignment helps. Avoid tiny type to fit more columns.
color: Separate brand accent from success, warning and failure. Combine semantic color with labels or shapes. Define selected, hover and focus independently; dark themes need their own tested pairs.
spacing: Offer comfortable defaults and a deliberate compact variant if users need it. Group toolbar controls near their results. Use row padding rather than reducing line-height until text collides.
composition: Start with context header, task controls, main result and exception detail. A table may be better than a bento grid. Place secondary panels only where they support the primary operation.
imagery: Use real or explicitly fictional task data, useful diagrams and product evidence. Do not substitute an arbitrary glowing chart for a working interface.
iconography: One coherent functional set. Persistent text labels for unfamiliar tools. Reserve icon-only controls for well-understood actions with accessible names.
components: Tables expose units, column headers, sort state and empty results. Forms preserve values after error. Charts include time range, units, comparison context and accessible data alternatives.
interaction: Support keyboard flow, filter reset, loading/error/empty states and clear feedback. Bulk or destructive actions need confirmation appropriate to their consequence.
motion: State changes should feel prompt. Animate spatial continuity only when it helps track an item. Avoid continuous count-up effects on frequently visited dashboards.
mobile: Choose priority columns and a deliberate overflow region for genuinely two-dimensional tables. Keep page-level reflow. Put labels on scroll regions and ensure keyboard access.
accessibility: Use native table markup unless a true interactive grid is needed. Validate focus return after dialogs, announcements after updates and errors tied to their inputs.
mistakes: Charts with no units or timeframe
Green/red as the sole state cue
KPI tiles unrelated to any user decision
amateurish: A handsome shell filled with arbitrary statistics, duplicate charts and nonfunctional filters.
exceptional: Every number has context, exceptional states have recovery, and the information density matches the actual decisions users make.
implementation: Use minmax(0,1fr) for the content track, overflow:auto on a named table region, and shared number/date formatters. The original operations example implements filtering and an empty state.
libraries: Native tables and forms first; React Aria or Radix may help complex behavior. Evaluate virtualization only after data volume warrants it. A design system supplies behavior, not a compulsory look.
evaluation: Can a user identify the most urgent item and act on it?
Do filters change the underlying result and announce the change?
Are values interpretable without color or decorative charts?
evidence: Original design recipe; source-linked engineering constraints. Not a validated causal model of visual quality.
